newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria hopes to restart reactor in December.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria hopes to restart reactor in December.

text.p: Bulgaria hopes to restart its oldest Soviet-made reactor at Kozloduy in December after receiving positive preliminary results of analysis of the condition of its metal, energy officials said on Monday.

The chairman of the National Electricity Company, (NEC) Kozma Kuzmanov, said first results from the analysis of samples of the vessel's metal had triggered optimism for the reactor's safe operation in the future but the tests had not been finalised yet.
"The first results give us a base for hope that the vessel's metal is in good condition but they (the results) have not been fully finalised yet," Kuzmanov told Reuters.

Officials from Russia's Korchatov Institute, which designed the plant and is analysing samples from its reactor number one, are expected to visit Sofia next week to present the results of the tests, NEC officials said.
They said the analysis had been carried out under the quality control of Germany's Siemens AG.

Bulgaria, which lacks energy resources and relies on all six Kozloduy reactors, will be on the edge of a power crisis in January if its oldest 440-megawatt reactor cannot come on stream by the year-end, they added.

The reactor, which was switched off in May amid international concern over its safety, will be restarted in December if it is found to be safe. But if results show that the metal needs thermal treatment, then the reactor will not be in operation this winter.
The Kozloduy 3,760-megawatt power plant provides around half the country's electricity needs.
